summary: cap_clip() measures the polygon's deepest violation of the plane (deep = max over vertices of -dir * ((xmaj ? P[i].y : P[i].x) - bound)) and returns np with P and T untouched when deep < 0.5. The expression matches both call sites: call 1 passes bound = floor(min(m) - w/2), dir = +1 and keeps coord >= bound, so the violation is bound - coord; call 2 passes bound = ceil(max(m) + w/2) + 1, dir = -1 and keeps coord <= bound, so the violation is coord - bound. Both bounds are integers by construction, and the early-out is the identity.

summary: The deadband's 0.5 is half a GUEST pixel, but the rasteriser samples DEVICE pixels. geom_line_params() (vk/draw.c:2756-2786) states in its own comment that the geometry stage works in guest pixels and that one guest pixel is surface_scale_factor device pixels, and divides by that factor to produce lineTieBias; out[2] = line_width / 8.0f is guest pixels too, and glsl/vsh.c uses surface_scale_factor only to scale oPts, never the vertex position. Device sample centres are therefore 1/scale apart in guest coordinates and the nearest one to an integer guest bound is 0.5 / scale guest pixels away, not 0.5. The comment at :548-559 states 'The nearest centre to an integer bound is half a pixel away, so the removed sliver of a shallower cut provably contains no sample' as a proof, without the surface_scale_factor == 1 hypothesis it needs. The shader does not read the scale, which is available -- lineTieBias already carries it.
scenario: g_config.display.quality.surface_scale is the user-facing Rendering Scale (vk/surface.c:92-100, menu at ui/xui/main-menu.cc:749-762). Set it to 2 and draw the Line_width suite. A cap overhang of 0.4 guest pixels past the low bound is skipped by the deadband (0.4 < 0.5), so the footprint keeps the corner and lights the device sample at guest coordinate bound - 0.25, which lies in guest pixel index bound - 1 -- the pixel the derived cap rule says must be dark. Measured over the same 48 non-void captures by counting plane violations in [0.5/scale, 0.5), the clips the shipped deadband skips and a device at that scale would have sampled: 191 plane-clips over 26 captures at scale 2, 293 over 29 at scale 3, 338 over 30 at scale 4. At scale 2 the affected captures run from Line_0010.0 to Line_0063.7, including every capture from Line_0024.0 up where the clip is the point of the change. MEDIUM and not HIGH because the error is one-directional: 0.5 > 0.5/scale for every scale >= 1, so the deadband only ever suppresses too much clipping, never too little; a suppressed clip emits master's own four corners, so no configuration is made worse than master, N1's re-quantisation cannot return through this, and there is no crash or unsafety. What is lost is part of #13's improvement at Rendering Scale > 1, silently, under a comment saying it cannot be lost.
remediation: Either: (1) scale the deadband to 0.5 / surface_scale_factor in guest units -- the shader lacks the scale today and lineParams is a full vec4, so this costs a push-constant component, and instance.c warns that the range is declared on every graphics pipeline; or (2) keep 0.5, since the direction is safe, and state the precondition in geom.c -- half a guest pixel, exact at surface_scale_factor == 1 and conservative above it, with the cost above it being the table in the pass-2b record. docs/testing/line_extent_subpixel.py already takes a --scale argument documented as 'surface_scale_factor; one guest px is this many ...', so the lane's own toolbox has the fact the derivation missed. Neither option need cost the pending arm: the harness pins surface_scale = 1 (desktop_channel.sh:454), so option 1 reduces to 0.5 at the scale the arm runs at and option 2 touches no code. If the fix is provably a no-op there, say so on the PR and let the queued arm on 36e85c96c9 stand rather than re-registering, which would restart a ~90-minute arm for a change the device cannot see.
